en: One who bore the people’s burden,
He raised his valor to the sky,
His stratagem drove them into the earth,
None remained to surrender the treasure,
The giving of all was shattered,
They fell before his valor,
Do not ask how fiercely he thundered,
With difficulty the grave mound collapsed,
Their sword points divided them,
The myriad Chinese fled.
He carried out the deed by hire,
The twisted Chinese Chongteñir,
Stood red with blood,
He set a snare toward the place of horses,
He drove the flock toward the warriors,
The innocent people spoke of this crime,
His gaze was a snare of doom,
He himself frightened the horses,
That Ozu Khan belonged to the enemy,
Standing alone upon the neck of the earth,
Hero Ebegey from captivity,
It was the time they surrounded him.
Hero Jeljetpes took the prison,
He stood alone among seven,
To the champion named at first,
The hero struck him in the face,
Upon the stones by his brow,
He came punching through,
Against the huge beastlike champion,
Blood poured out in abundance,
The long spear passed through him,
His life left mingled with blood,
The people struck beneath the blue night,
Drawing close, he leveled his bullet,
Tears flowed from both eyes,
His chest tightened with resolve,
The people struck beneath the blue night,
Baring his fangs, he roared,
The fortunate one had a snowy majesty,
If he pursued them, none would remain,
His elder, hero Ebegey,
He called, “Now gather them.”
A heroic warrior, a blue-maned lion,
Would the arrow not reach the grave?
At that time the Kergündör,
Were champion souls in combat,
The stones beneath their tread rang out,
Stones boomed like a great cauldron,
They shrieked above his crown,
He was a troubled hero,
He set himself against the troubled foe,
His mouth opened wide between them,
White foam mingled with blood,
From the thoroughbred he mounted for battle,
It struck him in the chest,
Then Kenen’s,
Blue-maned valor became clear,
Against the furious infidel host,
Against warrior Khan Ozu,
His figure loomed like a mountain,
Your shield was whole upon your head,
He thrust through toward the Kyrgyz.
The wrath of Jeljetpes,
Against hero Ozu Khan,
Truly found victory,
The two youths struck,
To settle the ancient feud,
Ebegey and Jeljetpes,
Spoke wrathfully of the contest,
When summoned to sacrifice,
Hero Kenen stood among seven,
A steel shield above his head,
Of warrior Ozu Khan,
Against the furious infidel host,
Together their hands struck through.
The inherited champion, Zhelzhetpes,
His splendor and menace filled the open plain,
His strength had been forged in heat,
He had the dark fittings hammered out,
He had it mounted in leather,
Its curled ornament was finely worked,
It roared like a dark living soul,
He had it bound in leather,
And fitted with a gold-wound haft,
Set upon grass, it sent fire racing,
Where its head was swung, embers flew,
When he swung it in fury,
It never returned without drinking blood,
Its edge glowed red with fire,
It had a somewhat short haft,
When he swung it in rage,
It stretched to a full fathom,
Those who saw its fury panicked,
Those who heard its name grieved,
The many foes who came face-to-face,
Despaired of their mortal lives,
The blood-spilling axe,
He seized and swung around,
Gripping it with both hands, he thrust with all his strength,
At Odukan, huge as a mountain,
The infidel of extraordinary strength,
The warrior never sated with blood,
Calling him the very spawn of fire,
Calling him the black eye of doom,
Calling him the face of the black eagle,
Aiming at his blue-clad neck,
He took careful aim and struck,
He swung with perfect accuracy.
No word fulfilled the wish,
For the beast that had been dragged three times,
It struck its tip and settled there,
The world fell upon the beast,
A great uproar rose among the survivors,
The earth seemed to collapse at the ears,
It lowered its head into the depths,
Dust filled the air,
Packing into its own nostrils,
Not a fly-sized scrap of life remained,
My hero's flesh was like dust,
It found its balance and struck,
God granted it to the Kyrgyz,
Such a deed as the world had witnessed,
There was a wrathful one, and there was his khan,
The whole massed army was there,
There was a clenched fist and a strong waist,
There was a renowned son of Tengir,
No one could fathom him,
Words could not fully describe him,
A master of the spear and of stratagem,
One who demanded the day from the stallion,
A choice remaining bronze spear,
Was there a hero like Chyng Tengir,
His wrestler who lay against the enemy,
Soz Khan hunted amid the plunder,
The coming voice was Chyng Tengir's,
He cast them down in heaps,
Countless wrestlers closed around,
Leaving none who drew a bow,
When the command came from his people,
He assembled a host of many falcons,
After he issued this command,
Folding his arms and cutting off heads,
God struck down his army,
The beast arose and showed its valor.
A cloud of majesty arose,
The rear-guard champion Jooshuk,
His strength was famed among the host,
Then the warrior crouched low,
A champion emerged among a thousand,
Known among every people,
All the Kyrgyz fell into uproar,
They leveled their spears firmly,
The earth split in that hour,
Every tethered horse stood ready,
Dust rose so thick the eye could not see,
If you saw it, smoke and flame filled the conflict,
The Kyrgyz stood alone, a gathered host,
The measured ground could not contain them,
Their spears could not reach their limit,
The dear Kyrgyz, a mighty army,
The day boiled with the massed foe,
A thousand Chinese against one Kyrgyz,
When he struck, he dragged them aside,
He scattered blood across the great host,
A single soul remained alive,
They swarmed like ants,
The earth turned slick beneath the trampling,
Chinese troops attacked from every side,
They came back from ages past,
The foe died and the feud remained,
Wrath stretched long,
The enemy remained upon the dear earth,
When the Chinese engulfed them,
In a brief stormy moment,
When distress descended upon their heads,
Calling it grief that came from China,
At the place where they clashed,
The warriors stood firm-kneed,
They never took their eyes from the hero,
Upon the head of the one who emerged,
They honored his glory.
The warrior Odukan appeared immense,
He hastened with immeasurable strength,
He had burning fury and flame,
An enemy life was fixed in his thoughts,
His rising rage scorched living souls,
Now it was Ebegey above all,
They prayed he might find a stratagem,
Saying that death is kin to every mortal,
One who could restore a life nearly severed,
When they hewed at one another squarely,
He could scatter four thousand at the pass,
They said the warrior was left like an old man,
Toward the Kerik standing ready,
They mounted Zhelzhetpes upon it,
Rousing his spirit and setting him upright,
His death-defying comrades stood with him,
Showing the victory of a hero,
He fell into hands filled with misfortune,
The warrior Zhelzhetpes burned with anguish,
From among the multitude of warriors,
A swelling conflict began,
Kögöy’s precious life hung by a thread,
Kenen entrusted the fallen one to them,
His life, tiny as a fly, grew faint,
His eyes burned as he faced the true world beyond,
The wrathful enemy formation was broken,
The great and numerous Kyrgyz people,
Precious Kenen and Ebegey,
The four stood and greeted one another,
Infidel and Muslim alike,
Do not forget the turmoil if you seek it,
Rage stirred up the rebellion,
They waged a fierce conflict,
Mounted on Kerik, he raced through the dust,
Taking the road toward safety,
He escaped out of the turmoil.
From the thunder with which he entered,
From the furious Chinese host,
A rare one who became a lion,
Burning with difficulty,
Seeing it, he gave his word,
Today my father summons me,
He stood while the day settled,
Behind you was a day of peace,
He was a son who knew the prayer,
To China he was red poison,
To the Kyrgyz he was their destined banner,
When he struck the foe amid the dust,
May God grant him to the Kyrgyz,
The ravine split and the cliff collapsed,
He laid waste the broad land,
Making his battle spirit known,
Their arms thrashed as they met,
Clouds covered the mountain,
Across low ridges and open plain,
They surged apart in wrath,
As though digging lightning from the sky,
Spurring horses, the seal fell,
Finish them; do not fear,
I shall crush and drag them away,
He aligned the stones and pressed in,
Every living creature,
Grew still and then trembled,
Thunder spread far and wide,
From fighting he could no longer see,
The people’s lament knotted within,
Every creature that came to mind,
Appeared while still alive,
The creatures upon the earth,
The ember in their breasts tightened,
He drove the foe straight through,
Across the drifting haze and cliffs.
Taking a bare, round stone,
With a bent rope twisted back,
Taking hide and piling it layer upon layer,
